title: AuthorAsOfResult
description:
`author.as_of` result: the point-in-time projection `check::slot_state_at`
derives for one `(pred, subject)` fluent slot, kernel-side — never routed
through `dli_eval::world::World::query_with` or the saturated derived
layer (the DL-0081/DL-0082 hard invariant). A `(pred, subject)` with no
fluent timeline answers with empty `holdings`, no fallback to the raw
extensional facts.

at.description: The query point's name, echoed back.

capping.description:
Whether that declaration is certain under the staged world's
valuation, so the projection is actually inertia-shaped rather than
byte-identical to the plain open-interval projection.

contested.description:
Whether two or more distinct values hold certainly at `at` at once —
[`dli_time::fluent::FluentState::has_contradiction`] over this same
projection.

holdings.description:
The values whose span could be in force at the query point, each with
its factorial verdict and, when capped, the defeater that bounds it.

inertial_citations.description:
The inertia declaration's own decision citations; empty when `pred`
was never declared inertial.

root_hash.description:
The workspace digest the read was evaluated against (`jcs:sha256:`
regime — the staged world is workspace state, not a store commit).
Like [`AuthorQueryResult::root_hash`], this names workspace state.

subject.description: The subject, canonicalized through the identity map.

AsOfDefeater.description: The certain, distinct competitor that defeats a capped [`AsOfHolding`].

citations.description: The defeater span's own decision citations.

since.description:
The defeater's `since` — the same point as the capped holding's
derived `until`.

AsOfHolding.description:
One [`AuthorAsOfResult`] value's standing at the query point: its
factorial verdict, its temporal anchors, and — for a capped inertial value
— the competitor that defeats it.

citations.description: The originating span's own decision citations.

defeater.description:
The certain, distinct competitor that caps this value (inertial only,
present exactly when [`Self::until`] is a derived rather than authored
boundary).

support.description:
The support half: the anchoring ruling's standing (dead spans are
dropped, never reported as a holding).

temporal.description:
The temporal half: whether the span's interval covers the query
point.

Projection.description:
The cautious three-valued temporal projection of a fluent onto a query point
(`docs/spec/03-time.md` §2). This is the *collapsed* reading of the factorial
verdict; the authoritative form is the `(cover × support)` pair on a
[`Holding`], which [`Holding::projection`] folds into one of these.

oneOf.description:
An initiator certainly precedes the query point, no terminator possibly
intervenes, and the anchoring ruling is certain.

It may hold — the anchoring ruling is merely possible (an unratified
order or fact), though the temporal cover itself is settled.

The answer turns on an order no one has declared: the query point is
unordered against one of the span's anchors. Repair by declaring a
`before`-fact.

Status.description: A claim's three-valued standing under `(ν, Θ)`, derived — never stored.

oneOf.description:
Every monomial is `Θ`-unsatisfiable: the claim holds in no admissible
world. (Whether this is rejection or mere supersession is a `C`
question, outside the algebra.)

Some monomial is `Θ`-satisfiable but none is resolved-and-undefeated: the
shadow layer.

Some monomial holds on resolved events alone, with that monomial's own
defeater not fully ruled: assertable.

TemporalCover.description:
The pure-order half of the factorial verdict: does the span's interval cover
the query point, reckoned by precedence alone? A span that certainly does not
cover the point yields no cover at all (it is dropped from
[`FluentState::holdings`]).

oneOf.description:
The initiator certainly precedes the point and no terminator does: the
interval certainly contains it.

The query point is unordered against an anchor, so whether the interval
contains it depends on an undeclared order.
